title: CJMC
text:
The Canada Jay Mathematical Competition (CJMC) is a national 90-minute multiple-choice math contest for students in grades K–8. It is a traditional fall activity usually hosted in late October or November. It has 15 multiple-choice questions. The questions are split into 3 blocks of 5 questions each, scaling progressively from approachable warm-ups to highly challenging logic puzzles. The test is scored out of 80 total points.

Format[edit]

The CJMC features a total of 15 questions split into three distinct difficulty tiers, adding up to a maximum score of 80 points. The exam begins with five introductory questions (Q1–Q5) and five intermediate questions (Q6–Q10), with each correct answer in these two tiers worth 5 points for a subtotal of 25 points per section. The final tier consists of five advanced questions (Q11–Q15) that scale up to 6 points each, accounting for the remaining 30 points of the total exam score. A blank answer gets one point, and a wrong answer gets nothing, that is the format after 2022. The version before 2022 is similar, except with 4 points each for the five introductory questions (Q1–Q5), 5 points each for the five intermediate questions (Q6–Q10), and 7 points each for the five advanced questions (Q11–Q15)
